changes.before: Why is deleting all conflict-marker lines alone insufficient?
changes.after: Resolve a merge conflict by deciding what the combined change should do, then checking it.

before: A merge conflict means Git could not automatically combine some edits. Choosing one side without understanding both changes can discard useful work.
One branch changes a greeting to Hello, Mira. Another adds an exclamation mark. The intended combined result might be Hello, Mira! rather than either branch’s exact line.

```bash
git status
git diff
# Edit the conflicted file after reviewing both intentions.
git add greeting.txt
git diff --cached -- greeting.txt
```

status identifies unmerged paths. diff helps inspect the conflict. Editing removes conflict markers and constructs the intended content. add records the resolution in the index; it does not prove the result works. Run the relevant check before completing the merge. Practice only in a disposable repository.
Changed situation: Why is deleting all conflict-marker lines alone insufficient?
A syntactically clean file can still lose behavior. Review both intentions and verify the result.
after: A merge conflict means Git cannot combine some edits on its own. Choosing one side blindly can throw away useful work.
Suppose one branch adds Mira's name to a greeting and another adds an exclamation mark. The wanted result may be Hello, Mira!, keeping both intentions.

In a disposable repository with a conflict in greeting.txt, follow these steps. Pause at the comment to edit the file before running git add.

```bash
git status
git diff
# Edit the conflicted file after reviewing both intentions.
git add greeting.txt
git diff --cached -- greeting.txt
```
status identifies the conflicted file. diff shows the changes. After editing the wanted result, add stages the resolution. diff --cached lets you inspect that staged result.
Conflict markers show where Git needs help. Removing those marker lines does not prove the remaining text or code is correct.
Check that the final result keeps the intended behavior. Run relevant tests before completing the merge. A file can look clean and still lose an important change.
